questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence:
The ________ of the school announced new guidelines for students.
questions.explanation: B is correct. PRINCIPAL (noun) = the head of a school or institution; also means main/primary as an adjective. PRINCIPLE (noun) = a fundamental rule, belief, or value. Memory trick: the principal is your 'pal'; a principle is a rule. Trap: 'principle of the school' would mean a rule/belief belonging to a school, not its leader.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The new tax policy will ________ all citizens equally.
questions.explanation: B is correct. AFFECT (verb) = to have an impact on; to influence. EFFECT (noun) = the result or consequence; occasionally used as a verb meaning 'to bring about'. In this sentence, 'will ________ all citizens' requires a verb → AFFECT. Memory: AFFECT = Action (verb); EFFECT = End result (noun). Trap: 'effect all citizens' would mean 'bring all citizens into existence' — nonsensical in context.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The red and blue colours ________ each other beautifully in the painting.
questions.explanation: B is correct. COMPLEMENT = something that completes or pairs well with something else (enhances or completes). COMPLIMENT = an expression of praise or admiration. 'Colours complement each other' = they go well together, enhancing the overall effect. Memory: COMPLEMENT = Complete; COMPLIMENT = praise. Trap: 'compliment each other' would mean the colours were praising each other (absurd in context).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
All students, ________ those who arrived late, were given participation certificates.
questions.explanation: B is correct. EXCEPT = excluding; not including (preposition). ACCEPT = to receive or agree to (verb). The sentence means 'all students excluding those who arrived late' → EXCEPT. Memory: EXCEPT = EXclude; ACCEPT = Agree. Trap: 'All students, accept those who arrived late' would mean the students accepted the late-comers — completely different meaning.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The shop was closed because the vendor had run out of ________.
questions.explanation: B is correct. STATIONERY (noun) = paper, pens, envelopes, and other writing materials sold in a shop. STATIONARY (adjective) = not moving; remaining in one place. The sentence is about a shop selling writing materials → STATIONERY. Memory: stationERY = lettERS (paper for letters); stationARY = stAY (staying in place). Trap: 'run out of stationary' — cannot 'run out of' an adjective.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The government was ________ to criticism for its handling of the crisis.
questions.explanation: D is correct. AMENABLE = open and responsive to suggestion; willing to accept or agree. 'Amenable to criticism' = receptive to being criticized. Trap: EMINENT = famous and respected; IMMINENT = about to happen soon; IMMANENT = inherent (philosophical term). None of these fit the context of 'open to criticism.'

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The inspector found several ________ activities at the construction site.
questions.explanation: B is correct. ILLICIT (adjective) = forbidden by law or rules; illegal. ELICIT (verb) = to draw out a response or reaction; to evoke. 'Illicit activities' = illegal/forbidden activities at the site. Memory: iLLiCiT = iLLegaL; eLiCiT = Evoke. Trap: 'elicit activities' is ungrammatical — ELICIT is a verb and cannot directly modify a noun without a participle form.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The diplomat was ________ in all his dealings, careful never to reveal classified information.
questions.explanation: B is correct. DISCREET (adjective) = careful and prudent, especially to avoid causing offence or revealing information. DISCRETE (adjective) = separate and distinct; individually distinct. 'Discreet in all his dealings' = careful and tactful. Memory: disCREET = taCT (tactful); disCRETE = separaTE (separate). Trap: 'discrete in all his dealings' would mean 'individually distinct in his dealings' — doesn't make contextual sense.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
Dr. Singh is an ________ economist whose work has influenced global trade policy.
questions.explanation: B is correct. EMINENT = famous and respected, especially in a particular field; distinguished. 'An eminent economist whose work influenced global policy' = a highly respected, well-known expert. Trap: IMMINENT = about to happen very soon (threat/event, not a person); IMMANENT = inherent or present throughout (philosophical); EMANATE = to originate from or be emitted from (a verb, not an adjective for a person).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
Please ________ the relevant legal document to support your claim.
questions.explanation: C is correct. CITE (verb) = to quote or refer to as evidence or example; to acknowledge a source. 'Cite the legal document' = reference/quote from it. Trap: SITE (noun) = a location or place (website, construction site); SIGHT (noun/verb) = the ability to see, or to see/spot something. 'Site the document' or 'sight the document' are both meaningless in context. SSC frequently tests cite/site/sight as a three-way confusion.
